paragraphs.text: Let your dsh freely invoke any agent or model to review.
# dsh-review
**English** | 中文

Code review as a tool, not a single vendor. Hand your diff to a CLI coding agent, or to a
subagent r
unning a model from your DSH configuration — then read one merged report.
## What it gives you

- **Two kinds of reviewer, both real agents.** `codex` / `claude` / `gemini` / `opencode` /
`cursor`

/ any CLI you template yourself, or a DSH subagent running a model from your DSH
configuration.
- *

*Several reviewers, one report.** They run in parallel; each gets its own section, in the
order they

were selected.
- **Review modes.** Name a strength and a prompt once (`quick`, `balanced`, `deep`,

…) and reuse
it, instead of retyping review instructions every time.
- **Configured in the GUI, and

saved for you.** Tick the reviewers you want; everything else
stays collapsed under advanced setting

s. Edits are written about a second and a half after you
stop typing — a status line at the top says

where they stand, and a **Save now** button remains
as a manual retry.
- **Review status, at a glan

ce.** Once there is a conversation, a slim line between it and the
composer says whether this sessio

n has reviewed, which round is running, how many rounds
finished, and who reviewed. Expand it for ea

ch round's time, scope, and outcome. It stays
hidden while the conversation is empty or when the cur

rent turn changed no files. The data is
session-scoped and persists across reloads.
- **No keys, no

endpoints.** Providers and credentials stay in your DSH config — this plugin
only asks for what is a

Providers and credentials stay in your DSH config — this plugin
only asks for what is already there.
## Install
Clone it somewhere permanent, then install it into a profile:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Or ask your agent to run `plugin_manager` → `install_bundle` with that absolute path.
Restart the host afterwards. Updating works the same way: `git pull`, then restart.

Requires **DSH 0.2.1 or newer**. The plugin declares this as `engines.dsh` in its manifest, so an
ol
der host refuses to install or activate it instead of failing later inside a review.
## Use
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Reviewing takes minutes, so the call waits a little and then hands back a job id: read the
result wi

th `job_output`, stop it with `job_kill`, or just wait — you are notified when it
settles.

Reviewers are opt-in: if nothing is enabled, a call with no `reviewers` fails and says so
rather tha

n quietly running everything. `timeoutMs` caps a single call; it is combined with the
configured `ha

rdTimeoutMs` by taking the smaller value, and the report attributes the timeout to
the limit that ac

by taking the smaller value, and the report attributes the timeout to
the limit that actually fired.
## Review status
A slim status line sits between the conversation and the composer, no panel required:
| State | What it shows |

| Nothing reviewed | `Review · Not reviewed yet` |
| Running | `Review · Round 2 in progress · 1m 05

s` + the running reviewers |
| Finished | `Review · 3 round(s) reviewed` + reviewer chips |
| Last r
ound failed/interrupted | `Review · Round 3 failed` / `Round 3 interrupted` |

Click the line for the last 30 finished rounds (plus any still running): round number, time,
scope (

uncommitted changes / a base branch / a commit), reviewers, and outcome. The round count
is not limi
ted by the retained history.

The data is a session projection: each `review` job writes once on registration and once on
settleme

nt, and the value is checkpointed with the session. Switching sessions, reloading, or
restarting the

host keeps the history. A round left running by a previous host process is shown
as `interrupted` i
nstead of ticking forever.
**When it stays hidden:**

- The conversation is still empty — no messages and no first turn in flight.
- The current turn chan

ged no files. This reuses the official
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-workspace-changes` plugin:
its `workspace/c

hanges` event is normally only appended for a turn that actually changed files, so the
status line d

oes not run its own `git status`. It remains visible while a turn is in progress
or a review is runn

ing, so triggering a review does not make it vanish.
- If the host does not mount `workspace-changes

`, only the empty-conversation rule applies; a
[该节后续省略]
## Known limitations

- Reviews always run in the **session's working directory**; you cannot point them elsewhere.
- One

call reviews one scope (uncommitted / a base branch / a commit), matching the underlying
CLIs. `base

` and `commit` are mutually exclusive. A range plus `instructions` works for
subagents but not for t

he codex CLI (its range flag and PROMPT exclude each other): if every
selected reviewer is such a CL

I the call is rejected up front, otherwise the CLI ones are named
in the report footnotes. To keep b

oth the range and the focus, add a subagent reviewer; putting
the focus in a mode's `prompt` does no

t help, since a mode prompt is skipped as well whenever a
range is given (next bullet).
- A mode's p

rompt reaches codex only when no range is given (its CLI refuses both at once); the
range is always

honoured, and the report says when the prompt was skipped.
- codex only runs inside the directories

it trusts (`~/.codex/config.toml`).
- An invalid `base`/`commit` fails before any reviewer starts, i

nstead of running for minutes and
reporting a batch that reviewed nothing.
- Report scaffolding (hea

dings, footnotes, errors) is Chinese; `language` only controls the
reviewers' own instructions.
- Tr

uncated reports stay in `$TMPDIR/dsh-review-*/report.md`; other runs clean up after
themselves.
- Me

rge commits are reviewed as the **first-parent** diff (`git show -m --first-parent`): that is
what t

he merge brought onto the current branch, not a combined diff.
- Untracked symbolic links are not fo

llowed, so a link cannot pull content from outside the
repository into the reviewer; the report list

s the names and says they were skipped.
- The "changed files preview" in the report header comes fro

m Git's file list; it describes the
scope, not proof that a reviewer inspected every file.
- The rev

iewer list in the tool description is a **registration-time snapshot**: the host does not
reload plu

gin code when the profile's dependencies change (measured: `patchReload: live` only
reloads the patc

h layer), so the description can lag behind disk. Use
`review({ doctor: true })` for the current tru

th. For the same reason, plugin code changes need
[该节后续省略]
